reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: The phases you learn are a bit out there. They talk about people cheating, girls being too big, and other items not relevant to first learning. You will also lose items that you made, making it hard for you to progress through the game. One day I left the game with a number of items being made then when I picked up again everything was gone; not in the inventory or complete, just gone.

reviews.title: Gamers unite!!
reviews.text:
If you love gaming, and want to learn a language this app is for you! It’s great that I can switch between working on the farmstead or go battling in adventure mode, depending on my mood for the day. It’s like farmville and deck building/battling all in one. All the while learning a language!

I’m especially happy with not having to feel pressure to keep up with a streak, or make place on the leaderboard. While it is fun to be competitive and unlock a couple extra rewards, it’s not at ALL necessary to enjoy the game unlike some others I have used.

reviews.title: This game is genuinely amazing
reviews.text: Good fun AND legit language practice

reviews.title: Cute but not able to stay engaged
reviews.text: It’s a cute game with a different take on language learning, but it feels more game-focused than actually learning-focused. The learning sessions are very minimal and repetitive, and you can only do 4 practice sessions (which take about a minute each) before you run out of energy, and you can only replenish energy by watching ads so many times. I don’t want to invest in premium when the free version didn’t impress me enough, so I can’t attest to the premium features.

reviews.title: Chill and helpful!
reviews.text: I especially love how it helps with spelling. I don’t get that on DuoLingo. I’ve been learning my language for a bit over a year and have been looking for a good addition to my learning, and this has been incredible so far!! No ads shoved in my face (they’re an option if you want to do things longer, but don’t randomly pop up and interrupt) and the ability to switch what I’m doing had been great. The storyline is fun, too! Kudos to you devs, you’re doing great. I normally am not one to leave reviews, but I feel like I struck gold here and just have to share!!

reviews.title: Great but app has problems
reviews.text: Looking to learn in a simple form this is a great way to do it. But the app does have problems logging progress premium members or people considering premium perks please be aware that some of your progress will not be awarded or revoked when logging in later.

reviews.title: Deleting hard to navigate
reviews.text: I want to change to a different language and it seems impossible because there’s no way to get to the options. You’re just stuck in the screen where you’re learning in the barn and you can’t get back to your options.

reviews.title: Love Lingo Legend
reviews.text:
This is easily my favorite language-learning app so far. The gameplay is genuinely fun and educational, the pacing feels just right, and the whole experience seems thoughtfully designed and fairly priced.

I’m currently learning Japanese, and I especially appreciate being able to switch to “review” mode whenever I want to pause new material and reinforce what I’ve already learned. The kana practice has been surprisingly effective—my hiragana recognition has noticeably improved since I started playing.

It also complements the other tools I use, like audiobooks and conversational practice. The game starts simply and introduces new material at a comfortable pace, so I feel like I’m actually building on what I know instead of being overwhelmed with new information.

Even though the side stories aren’t normally the type of thing I’d gravitate toward, they have been enjoyable. Overall, Lingo Legend has struck a great balance between being an actual game I want to play and a learning tool. 🩷

reviews.title: Great Game!
reviews.text: So much fun!!!! Definitely my favorite way to learn.

reviews.title: Fun but….
reviews.text: I really hate that you can’t turn off the spelling questions. I’m severely dyslexic so I love the format of this game for learning but we should absolutely be able to turn off the spelling questions.

reviews.title: Most helpful language learning app!!
reviews.text: This app has been the MOST helpful language app I have ever used BY FAR (and I’ve tried a lot)! The guild chat is not necessarily geared well toward actual conversation, but it’s still helpful for making new friends. I also want to request adding Russian! My friend would love to play too, but they don’t have the language she’s learning yet!

reviews.title: i love it!!!
reviews.text: one of the only language learning app that’s accessible without paying, and one of the only ones i would consider paying for!

reviews.title: Can’t get out of ads
reviews.text:
Update after dev response - in order to get the ads to work, you can’t just pause your VPN, you have to completely disconnect it in settings. Glad it works now, but it’s a hassle. Why do the ads need to know specifically where I am? :P

Original review:
I love the idea of gamifying language learning, but the energy system sucks unfortunately. I can watch the ads fine, but the X button doesn’t work. I can’t get back to the game after and have to close out the app after. Then the energy isn’t updated. So I watched an ad for free. :(

I’m on an iPhone 16 Pro running iOS 26.6.1. Hopefully this is fixed soon.

reviews.title: Adorable game

I can tell they put so much work and care into this, and there’s not a speck of AI in any of the artwork which is amazing to say the least. Thanks for the team behind Lingo Legend for making this awesome game! I love it

reviews.title: Awesome but am i learning?
reviews.text: This app is awesome, it's more motivating than any other language learning app I've used. I LOVE that there's no ads unless you want them, and that the language practice is made by real teachers instead of ai slop. But, i have a 57 day streak and I feel like I haven't learned anything? The format for practice is very easy to guess on. On the spelling ones, which should be the hardest, i can usually guess what the word is supposed to be based on the letters i have. It would be great to have more varied practice, like making us type the answer without getting the letters. Or  for example instead of just "the keys are on the table" every time, maybe the keys are somewhere else and we have to fill in the blank. Talking to the villagers in your target language would be cool too, to have a back and forth. Idk

reviews.title: Need more languages
reviews.text: I downloaded this app because I saw a Tiktok about it and how amazing it is, but when I downloaded it there was no option for Arabic which is the language that I am trying to learn I feel it has so much potential but really does need more options for languages I only gave a 1 because I want the Lingo Legend team to see this review and please add some more languages!!🙏

reviews.title: Amazing app, premium is overpriced
reviews.text:
I will start by saying that a premium membership is not necessary to use the app. But without premium you have a limited amount that you can play each day. You have to watch ads to replenish the “energy” you have for language practice sessions in order to progress in the game, and there are a limited number of ads you can watch per day. When I first started playing, I would run out of all the day’s ads within two hours of playing.

I decided to pay for the premium month-by-month for now, while the game is new and exciting and is grabbing my interest so much. I will say that the way the game practices language learning works AMAZINGLY for me. It really helps you practice every day without feeling like a chore. My main issue is that the premium is overpriced in my opinion. It’s either $10 a month, $60 for a year, or over $100 for a lifetime subscription. When I think of the fact that the average game on PC or console costs $20-60, I can’t justify paying such high prices for a yearly subscription or over $100 for lifetime use on a phone app. I understand that it’s a small team, but I think you’d get more people buying premium if it was cheaper. I would love to buy premium for my friends, but it’s outrageously expensive to even pay for my own premium, much less anyone else’s. I really wish the price was lower. If premium can’t be cheaper, then don’t limit the daily ads so much!

reviews.title: Thank you developers
reviews.text: My Spanish exponentially grew in less than two weeks compared to when I did a 100 days streak on the owl app. Seriously and genuinely thank you. I hope this app grows more popular.

reviews.title: Learning for All Ages!
reviews.text: This app gives learning a new language adventure! My household has been using it for about a month now and we can have simple conversations in Spanish! Very kid friendly and great for those that struggle with learning a new language!

It was good enough for me to buy the game, which turned out my biggest mistake. Now I played through the game, and it feels “done”. Yes, I can still practice my language skills, but there are’ r enough levels to justify to buy it.

Subjective obv, but I feel like the gear and characters are pretty generic or even bad while the rest of the game shines. If you could clean up the aesthetic this would be the best game on the market.

reviews.title: I suggest adding a "none of the above" option.
reviews.text:
When I select English as the language I want to learn, I need to pick my native language. The only choices are French and Spanish, and I speak neither. I have to choose one of them to proceed. Alright, I’m just going to pick one randomly to proceed. 
Therefore, I suggest adding a "none of the above" option.

reviews.title: Great bones with areas for improvement!
reviews.text:
I like the structure of the game so much that I’ve bought a membership! But some things I’ve noticed now that I’ve played a couple hours that could use improvement on.
1. Language units: I’m working on Chinese and I’m not sure if it’s just because Chinese is the less popular language to learn here but the greetings unit isn’t super comprehensive. It’s giving you phrases to memorize but doesn’t teach you the vocabulary for each word. Like good morning is zao shang hao, I know hao is good from a previous lesson but I don’t know what zao means or shang means. There’s also no way to know from the vocab cards either. They should implement different pre testing modes, like picking out the individual words to make up the phrase. 
2. Vocab cards: I think there should a library that builds up the more words you learn. There’s a custom library thing but that just requires me to manually move over words. This kinda ties into the first point too because if you learn the individual vocabs first, you can also put them together into phrases and it’ll be easier to recall. These phrases can also be put in the library after you’ve learned them.
3. There should be an option to flag a word that you’ve learned but can’t recall on the spot. So you can go back to your library and flag the word to be put in the learning rotation for something.
4. There should also be a test part that tests you on the words more effectively than just giving you the choices or having you spell out the Ping yi. But maybe that’s a later unit and I’m just jumping the gun.
5. This is kinda a nit picky thing but I wish the decorations could be placed closer together. Like the maple tree has a big placement surface area and it’s annoying cuz i can’t place flower patches closer together to the tree and it looks a little sparse and unnatural. Overall the aesthetics of the town building could be more refined. 

Either way great experience so far and hope improvements happen frequently!

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: No notes

reviews.title: Engaging way to learn!
reviews.text:
I’ve tried just about every language learning app out there, and this one surprised me. Lingo Legends somehow makes studying feel like playing a game instead of grinding through flashcards. It keeps me coming back, which is half the battle with language learning.

I’m studying Mandarin, and I’ve noticed I’m recognizing and remembering Chinese characters much faster than I was with more traditional apps. The combination of gameplay, repetition, and progression just clicks with the way I learn.

No app is going to magically make you fluent, but if an app can keep you engaged long enough to build a daily habit, that’s a huge win. Lingo Legends does exactly that. It’s earned a permanent spot in my language learning routine.

reviews.title: Phenomenal
reviews.text:
I rarely leave ratings, but,

I love how gamified it is; you can truly see all the soul and work the creators put into it. I have only used it for 2 days SO FAR, but it’s truly great. I would recommend it to anyone learning a new language!

reviews.title: Effective

reviews.title: Great game!

reviews.title: Watching ads doesn’t replenish stamina
reviews.text: I like the premise and this app seems promising, but i don’t like how i tried to watch ads 3 times to replenish stamina and it didn’t work.  I don’t mind watching ads to get stamina, but when it doesn’t work it limits how much you can do in this app.

reviews.title: Updated: Support Cares
reviews.text:
I had reached out to them to tell them that the space recognition only repeats the first few phrases and never seems to get beyond numbers.

They recognized there was an issue with this and informed me of both how to navigate the issue for now and that they have plans to roll out an update that fixes this so you don’t have to fix it the long way. 

The characters are incredibly well written and endearing and the art style is really good. While some mechanics are a bit repetitive, that does make the game pretty easy to follow as you progress. There are different ways to approach the learning with “Adventure” and “Farm” so if you get bored of one you can change up the pace for either classic mobile farm game style or adventure that treats combat similar to hearthstone which I thought was neat. 

Update released and fixed the issue!

reviews.title: Broke Students Opinion:
reviews.text: I downloaded this game because I’m constantly playing mobile games to keep myself busy between walking, conversations, social settings. I’m a slave to the quick dopamine my phone gives me. I wanted to find a game that at least helped me feel like I was gaining something meaningful to the real world. And then I found this app on a Facebook add of all places between all the A.I slop. I am so pleasantly surprised at the star-dew like farming and slay the spire card battler esc introduction to learning. The soft approach from vowels to consonants I’m a huge fan it felt nicely paced and the reinforcement and encouragement with new cards and learning is smooth. The arts very cozy I can see this becoming more favorable than some of the Pc or switch games I have on my shelf still. My only complaint is very small but the tips for moving things on the farm I felt would have been more helpful if it had appeared before placing the bakery instead of after. Otherwise I happily watch adds as learning has been invigorating and fun so far. I’m even considering saving up for a premium sub surprisingly enough. Tho like the title I’m a Broke student going to a local collage in pursuit of my GED so it might take a bit. I can see this app being a valuable tool in acquiring not only a wide verity of digestible linguistic skills. But in motivation for me becoming a new me academically. 5Stars from me Lingo team, thank you for sharing your hard work with people like me. I think what all of you are doing is wonderful. keep it up!

reviews.title: French Needs Work
reviews.text: I paid for a lifetime subscription and I am getting more and more frustrated with my decision by the day. The French course needs a lot of work and the staff is not taking it seriously.

reviews.title: Humble Creators
reviews.text:
I came in this app thinking I’d be hit with a subscription or a free trial and not be able to actually learn on the app for FREE. I thought maybe ad supported for free users at least like Duolingo? But no. It’s way better. The content is free and you’re not being bombarded with ads AT ALL. Not only that the creators after I do watch an ad, they say thanks for the support or something like that. And not only that when they asked me to review the game, they did it so kindly I just had to! 

The game itself is amazing I love the mechanics of it. You can do short or long sessions easy. It’s not boring and doesn’t feel repetitive. The app also allows you to customize your settings for a better learning experience. 

Overall the app is great and I’m so grateful to the creators! I’ll watch the ads because I don’t mind it and I get rewarded in the game with energy!

reviews.title: Amazing game overall
reviews.text: Really fun, all the features are well thought out and executed. The only reason I rated this game four stars is that it had a lack of language options. Please Lingo Legend team, if you’re seeing this, add Swedish lessons into the game!

reviews.title: Enjoyable
reviews.text: The game is well crafted and fun so far. It would be cool to have two separate farms to switch between if you want to do two languages at once.

reviews.title: So far, so good!
reviews.text: I haven’t been playing long, I’m only level 3, but I do feel like I’m learning and in a fun way! The premium costs are monthly and way too high, I’d happily pay a higher one-time price for premium content with possible micro transactions along the way, but without knowing how long I’ll play it, it’s too much to commit to for a monthly price. I am enjoying it, but still on what seems to be the first lesson. Will certainly update my review as is reasonable.

reviews.title: Incredible Setup, One Bug
reviews.text:
Absolutely love the way everything is laid out and how the learning is weaved into different aspects of the game, BUT I get this bug every 30 min or so where I can’t progress past a mission complete/next step screen. 

Would be a 5 if not for that, especially because the devs don’t use AI as far as I’m aware!!
